answers.q5: No weakening found in the pr-a/pr-b test diff. C1 and H3 changed from asserting platform.state === 'published' to 'retired' -- that is not a weakening, it restates the same field against the new correct value, and C1 adds new assertions (retired_at set, forkSource.version > platform.version) that did not exist before. E1 and G1's fork-count checks moved from the literals 42/142 to `templateCounts(forkSource.id)`, but this is not tautological: read clara.fork_coa_template's own body (0150:904-905), the door's returned `families`/`accounts` are counted from the NEW DRAFT's rows (template_id = the freshly forked copy), while `templateCounts(forkSource.id)` counts the SOURCE's rows -- two different template_ids, so a copy bug (dropped or duplicated rows) would still make the assertion fail. The literal the review worried about disappearing is still pinned elsewhere in the same file: C2 (packages/db/tests/coa-template-pr-a.test.mjs:297-301) asserts `templateCounts(platform.id)` (v1) equals the hardcoded 42/142 exactly, so 0150's fixed artifact is still literal-pinned, just under `platform` (v1) rather than `forkSource` (v2). In pr-b, the §5.2 mutant deletes moved from an unscoped `delete ... where entity_type='society' and account_code='3900'` to one scoped `and template_id = $1` (starter.id), and the closing census moved from a global `count(*) = 2` to a per-template count -- both changes narrow the blast radius and strengthen the assertion (a global count could have passed by counting v1's rows while v2's were silently empty, which was the exact defect S1 caught); neither is a weakening.
answers.q7: Only 0156_coa_apply_template.sql names my_sme_starter between 0151 and 0294 (grep confirmed; 0150 and 0295 are the two boundary files outside that range). 0156's own prestate (S0, lines 285-298) DOES assert the platform starter is state='published' before seeding its entity-override rows and event-type registration -- so if 0156 could be redone on a database where 0295 has already retired v1, that assertion would fail. But it cannot be reached: packages/db/scripts/migrate.mjs's redo path (lines 389-401) refuses to redo any migration that is not the HIGHEST currently-applied version ('redoing anything below the frontier would silently invalidate whatever was applied on top of it'). Once 0295 (or anything after 0156) has landed, 0156 is no longer the highest applied migration and CLARA_MIGRATION_REDO=0156_coa_apply_template is refused outright by the tool before 0156's own body ever runs. So the hazard is real in principle but structurally unreachable in practice, by a platform-wide rule 0295 did not need to know about. Separately, grep found packages/runtime has zero references to coa_templates or my_sme_starter, so nothing there can assert a version. apps/web's two list_coa_templates fixtures (onboarding-amend-and-chart.test.tsx:250 and e2e/agentic-finish-mock.mjs:339) DO hardcode `version: 1` as canned mock data, but neither is a live read of the lane database -- they are self-contained UI/e2e mocks that never talk to Postgres, so there is nothing for 0295 to have drifted out from under them. This is the same S5 nit the review already recorded and the fix report already answered ('a reading, not a run'); I found nothing beyond what was already disclosed.
answers.q8: Read 0156's apply_coa_template (0156:726-899) and found a LIVE instance of exactly this scenario already on the lane database: one coa_template_adoptions row (id c8415e59-...) sits in state='proposed', naming template_id af0d7c77-... (my_sme_starter v1, now state='retired') at template_version 1 -- a rig fixture from the pr-a/pr-b batteries, not real client data (0295 itself writes no row to coa_template_adoptions, confirmed by reading the whole file). 0295 neither refuses, converts nor deletes this row -- it is silently left exactly as it was. What happens next depends entirely on what template_id a later apply_coa_template call names: (1) if the caller/UI resubmits the SAME proposed template (p_template = v1's id), rung 4 (0156:768-771) refuses it BY NAME with `template_not_published` ('template my_sme_starter version 1 is retired, not published') before touching the adoption row at all -- a clean, named refusal, not a crash or silent corruption, and the stale 'proposed' row is untouched by the failed call. (2) if instead the caller applies against v2 (the new current template), rung 4 passes, and the existing generic 'Clara proposed X, human applied Y' logic at 0156:842-887 already handles the mismatch with no code change needed: since v_prop.template_id (v1) does not equal t.id (v2), the ELSE branch inserts a fresh 'adopted' row against v2 and marks the old v1 proposal 'superseded' (0156:884-886). Note that clara.wake_propose_coa_template_trim, the door 0150/0143 name as the intended writer of 'proposed' rows, was never actually built (grep of pg_proc and every migration found no such function) -- so today, on this lane database, 'proposed' rows only exist as direct test-fixture SQL, not through any real product door. This is a real release-preflight fact worth carrying into the wave's hosted checklist (any hosted client with a genuine pending proposal against v1 needs a re-propose/re-apply against v2, and will see a named refusal rather than a silent no-op if the old proposal is resubmitted as-is) but it is not a defect in 0295 or a gap the fix worker should have closed -- no ruling asked for an adoption-migration mechanism, and none exists elsewhere in the estate for exactly the reason 0295's own header states (0295:112-116, 'no door in the estate re-syncs').
